company.name: Northwind Software
company.description: A 300-person company that sells a project-management web app to business customers.

ticket.title: Problem with my team lead
ticket.description: My team lead keeps making comments about my age in meetings. I'd like to talk to someone about it confidentially.

main_department.instructions: Which team should own `ticket` and do most of the work on it?

criteria.it_support: Internal IT: employee laptops, accounts, passwords, VPN, email, software licences for staff. Not bugs in the product customers use.
criteria.engineering: The product team: bugs, errors, outages and performance problems in the web app that customers use, and requests for new product features.
criteria.security: Suspected phishing, leaked passwords or keys, unauthorised access, malware, and vulnerability reports.
criteria.finance: Invoices, payments, refunds, pricing and plan changes for customers, and supplier invoices. Not an employee's own salary or expenses.
criteria.hr: Anything about an employee's own job: salary, payslips, expenses reimbursement, leave, contracts, hiring, complaints about a colleague.
criteria.legal: Contracts with customers or suppliers, data-protection (GDPR) requests from customers, NDAs, legal threats.
criteria.sales: New customers asking to buy, demos, quotes, and existing customers asking to upgrade to a bigger plan.
criteria.facilities: The office building: desks, heating, cleaning, keys and access cards, meeting rooms, deliveries.

fits_a_department.instructions: Is `ticket` work that one of these teams does? it_support: Internal IT: employee laptops, accounts, passwords, VPN, email, software licences for staff. criteria.true: The ticket clearly matches the work of at least one listed team.
criteria.false: The ticket is about something none of the listed teams handle, or is empty or unreadable.

has_enough_detail.instructions: Does `ticket` say enough for the owning team to start work without asking the reporter a question first?

criteria.true: It says what happened or what is wanted, and where.
criteria.false: For example: only 'it doesn't work' or 'please help', with no hint of what or where.

is_confidential_personal_matter.instructions: Is `ticket` about the reporter's own pay, health, contract, or a complaint about a named colleague?

criteria.true: Something a person would expect only the responsible team to read.
criteria.false: A work request that anyone in the company could see without harm.

urgency.instructions: How many people does the problem in `ticket` stop from working?
criteria: Nobody is blocked; it can wait a week or more.
One person is slowed down but can keep working.
One person or one customer cannot do their work.
Many people or many customers cannot do their work.

ongoing_loss.instructions: Does `ticket` describe money or data being lost or exposed right now, so that more is lost every hour nobody acts?

criteria.true: For example: a secret still public online, customers being charged wrongly as it happens, records being deleted.
criteria.false: The harm already happened once and is waiting to be fixed, such as one past charge to refund, or there is no loss.
